title: Home Depot’s Comparable Sales Rose 2.2% Even as Customer Transactions Fell 0.5%. Here’s What’s Behind the Gap.
author: Eric Volkman
description: Home Depot reported Q3 2026 earnings that narrowly beat consensus estimates with $43.4B in sales (up 5% YoY) and comparable sales growth of 2.2%, despite a 0.5% decline in customer transactions. The gap was explained by a 3% increase in average ticket size, driven by strength in the B2B Pro division and categories like appliances and power tools. The company announced three C-suite leadership changes and narrowed full-year guidance on operating margins and EPS growth, which weighed on stock sentiment.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Despite initial negative market reaction (-2.45%), the article presents a net positive outlook. The company beat earnings estimates, grew comparable sales 2.2%, and demonstrated strength in sticky, higher-margin B2B and professional segments. The increase in average ticket size (3%) indicates customers are spending more per transaction. The author views the company as well-positioned for future growth if the housing market improves, recommending a bullish stance for mid- to long-term investors.

title: Home Depot Q3 Earnings Meet Estimates, Sales Beat on Comps Growth
author: Na
description: Home Depot reported Q3 fiscal 2026 adjusted EPS of $3.86, meeting estimates, with sales growing 4.9% to $43.4 billion. Comparable sales rose 2.2% driven by higher average ticket ($93.09), though customer transactions declined slightly. However, gross margin contracted 60 basis points to 32.8% due to cost of sales outpacing revenue growth. Operating margin also narrowed 30 basis points. Management updated FY26 guidance projecting 4.5% sales growth and 1.4% comparable sales growth.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Mixed results with EPS meeting estimates and revenue beating expectations, but offset by gross margin contraction of 60 bps and operating margin decline of 30 bps. Comparable sales growth of 2.2% is positive but driven by higher spending per customer rather than transaction volume growth, indicating softer customer traffic. Lowered FY26 guidance with comparable sales growth projected at only 1.4%.

title: Retail Sales Increased in Line with Expectations
author: Na
description: Markets showed mixed pre-market futures following Monday's decline across major indices. October retail sales slowed to +0.2%, while import prices exceeded expectations at +1.1%. Disney beat earnings expectations but shares fell on theme park slowdown concerns. Home Depot matched earnings estimates but faced declining store visits. NVIDIA is set to report Q3 earnings after market close amid uncertainty following CEO Jensen Huang's departure.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Company expected to report strong Q3 earnings (+92.31% YoY) with five consecutive beats, but significant uncertainty due to CEO Jensen Huang's recent departure overshadows positive fundamentals.
Beat earnings expectations with strong streaming and sports performance, but shares declined 1.3% due to investor concerns about slowing theme park visits forecasts.
Matched earnings consensus and raised prices, but shares fell 2.28% as store visits declined and the sluggish housing market outlook suggests continued weakness ahead.

title: Home Depot's Best Comp of the Year Arrives With a Thinner Margin
author: Na
description: Home Depot exceeded Q3 revenue expectations with $43.4B in sales (up 4.9%) and 2.2% comparable sales growth, but margins contracted significantly. Gross margin fell to 32.8% from 33.4% year-over-year, with the company guiding sales to the high end while margins move to the low end of guidance. The margin pressure stems from acquisition-driven growth through lower-margin professional distribution channels. Management also implied fourth-quarter comparable sales will decelerate to around 1% despite strong current momentum.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: While the company beat revenue expectations and showed resilience in a weak housing market, profitability metrics deteriorated significantly. Gross and operating margins contracted despite strong sales growth, indicating the company is 'buying growth rather than earning it' through acquisitions. Management guided margins to the low end of ranges while implying Q4 deceleration, suggesting limited near-term upside.

The article anticipates Lowe's will report similar negative trends as Home Depot, with revenue growth driven by acquisitions while earnings decline. The home improvement sector's signature pattern of revenue growth on acquisitions coupled with earnings shrinkage is expected to be confirmed by Lowe's earnings report.

title: Retail Sales & Disney Numbers This Morning, NVIDIA This Afternoon
author: Na

Disney beat earnings expectations but shares fell on theme park concerns, while Home Depot matched estimates but faced declining store visits.
